{{Short description|Formula in representation theory}}
In mathematical [[representation theory]], '''Steinberg's formula''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Steinberg|year=1961|authorlink=Robert Steinberg}}, describes the [[multiplicity (mathematics)|multiplicity]] of an [[irreducible representation]] of a semisimple complex [[Lie algebra]] in a [[tensor product]] of two [[irreducible representation]]s.
It is a consequence of the [[Weyl character formula]], and for the Lie algebra [[Special linear Lie algebra|sl<sub>2</sub>]] it is essentially the [[Clebsch–Gordan formula]].

Steinberg's formula states that the multiplicity of the irreducible representation of highest weight ''ν'' in the tensor product of the irreducible representations with highest weights ''λ'' and ''μ'' is given by

:<math> \sum_{w,w^\prime\in W} \epsilon(ww^\prime)P(w(\lambda+\rho)+w^\prime(\mu+\rho)-(\nu+2\rho))</math>

where ''W'' is the [[Weyl group]], ε is the [[determinant]] of an element of the Weyl group, ρ is the [[Weyl vector]], and ''P'' is the [[Kostant partition function]] giving the number of ways of writing a vector as a sum of positive roots.
